statement_record.book: Cayley's theorem: any group is isomorphic to a subgroup of a permutation group. Proof: regard G as a one-object category BG; the covariant Yoneda embedding carries its object to the right regular G-set G, and full faithfulness identifies G with the monoid of G-equivariant endomorphisms of that G-set, each of which is invertible, so G ≅ Aut(G_G); composing with the faithful forgetful functor to Set exhibits G as a subgroup of Sym(G).
statement_record.intree: Covariant_Yoneda_Embedding `(C : Category) : ∀ A B : C, Copresheaves [Hom B,─] [Hom A,─] ≊ A ~> B, together with Construction/Cayley.v's Cayley : Category (the image of that embedding as a standalone category) and the pair To_Cayley : C ⟶ Cayley, From_Cayley : Cayley ⟶ C.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger on the general theorem the corollary is an instance of — full faithfulness holds for EVERY category C, hence a fortiori for a one-object one; intree-weaker on everything specific to the corollary. Same-name-but-weaker trap flagged: the file named Construction/Cayley.v does NOT prove Cayley's theorem for groups. It states no group, no permutation group, no subgroup and no group isomorphism, and it never asserts that To_Cayley is faithful — there is no `Faithful To_Cayley` instance; the split-faithfulness claim From_Cayley (To_Cayley f) ≈ f appears only in the header comment (line 39), and the file's only lemmas, Cayley_Right/Cayley_Left (lines 179, 191), state the round trip in Leibniz `=` under the extra strict-unit hypothesis (∀ a b (k : a ~{C}~> b), id[b] ∘ k = k), which is a reassociation/difference-list fact, not an embedding theorem.

statement_record.book: Exercise 2.2.i: state and prove the dual of the Yoneda lemma — for a contravariant F : C^op → Set and c ∈ C, evaluating the component at c on id_c is a bijection Nat(C(−,c), F) ≅ Fc, natural in both c and F, whose inverse sends x ∈ Fc to the transformation carrying f : d → c to (Ff)(x).

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the exercise's bijection is proved outright, in exactly the dual shape, with the same forward map (evaluation at id) and the same inverse, as an isomorphism of setoids in Sets (setoid rephrasing with hom-setoids and ≈ is faithful; local smallness is carried by universe polymorphism rather than a size hypothesis). What is missing is the second clause of the statement being dualised — naturality in c and in F — which is asserted nowhere in the tree, only recorded as the comment 'natural in both A and F' at Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:22.

gap: Two precise gaps. (1) Naturality: exactly as for Theorem 2.2.4 (riehl:2.2:thm4), Yoneda_Lemma quantifies over A INSIDE the statement and takes F as a section parameter, yielding an unrelated family of Sets-isomorphisms; there is no statement that A ↦ (evaluation at id) is natural, nor that F ↦ (evaluation at id) is, and no packaging as an isomorphism in a functor category or of bifunctors. (2) The exercise's 'state the dual' content — deriving the contravariant form from the covariant one by the duality principle — has no in-tree counterpart: Yoneda_Lemma (line 133) and Covariant_Yoneda_Lemma (line 182) are two independent Program Instances with separately discharged obligations, neither obtained from the other by instantiating at C^op, even though Construction/Opposite.v:126's op_invol : (C^op)^op = C would license it.
